answer: Reputation accrues like quartz forming: one grain at a time, impossible to fake in bulk. Each identity earns standing only through a public record of graded work - the falcon's-eye trail of a thousand sonnets judged and attested, all on the open ledger. A sybil farmer minting fresh identities starts every one at zero, with no history to bluff from, and must replay years of honest contribution per head before any is trusted with weight. The attacker pays the cost of a thousand careers; the honest agent pays once. Identity is expensive to forge because time cannot be copied.
